newsitem.title: ST VINCENT: Americans' murder trial in St.Vincent delayed.
newsitem.headline: Americans' murder trial in St.Vincent delayed.

text.p: The murder trial of Americans James and Penelia Fletcher, accused of killing a St. Vincent water taxi operator, was delayed again until Wednesday as lawyers haggled over pre-trial publicity.
If convicted, they face death by hanging at a hilltop fort overlooking the Caribbean Sea.
Eastern Caribbean High Court Judge Dunbar Cenac on Monday granted a request by lawyers for the Fletchers for a delay while they filed counter-applications against prosecution motions.

The trial of James Fletcher, 49, former president of a Huntington, W.Va., mining equipment company, and his wife, Penny, 35, was to start last Wednesday. They were arrested and charged last October with the murder of water taxi driver Jerome "Jolly" Joseph.

The prosecution says the Fletchers and their lawyers have orchestrated a media smear campaign to discredit St. Vincent's legal system. It wants a gag order on trial coverage, adjournment of the trial, and secrecy for the jurors.

The Fletchers have been held in separate prisons since their arrests on Oct. 30. The couple retired last year to sail around the world on their 47-foot (14.3 metre) yacht. They arrived in St. Vincent and the Grenadines last fall.

Joseph, 30, ferried tourists from their boats to the island of Bequia, a prime Caribbean sailing destination near St. Vincent. On Oct. 6 he picked up the Fletchers for a late dinner. His bullet-riddled body was pulled from the water three days later.
